meta.description: {brand}'s data processing agreement (GDPR article 28) for businesses: how we process your customers' personal data on your behalf.

title: Data processing agreement
intro: When your customers book through {brand}, you decide how their data is used and we process it for you. This agreement sets out our obligations as your processor under article 28 of the GDPR. It is part of the Terms of service, so it applies to every account automatically.

s1.title: Parties and scope
s1.p1: This Data Processing Agreement (“DPA”) is between the business that has a {brand} account (the “Controller”, “you”) and <provider></provider> (the “Processor”, “we”). It forms part of the <terms>Terms of service</terms> and applies automatically, with no separate signature needed, whenever we process personal data on your behalf while providing {brand}.
s1.p2: Terms such as “personal data”, “processing”, “controller”, “processor”, “data subject” and “personal data breach” have the meaning given in Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (the “GDPR”). If this DPA and the Terms conflict on data protection, this DPA prevails.

items.i1: Subject matter and purpose: providing {brand} to you: hosting your booking page, taking and managing bookings, storing customer records, sending appointment emails on your behalf, statistics, exports and support.
items.i2: Duration: for as long as you use {brand}, and until the data is deleted as described below.
items.i3: Nature of processing: collection through the booking page or your entries, storage, organisation, retrieval, display to you and your team, transmission by email, export and erasure.
items.i4: Data subjects: your customers and prospective customers who book or whom you add; your staff and team members.
items.i5: Categories of personal data: name, email address, phone number, appointment details (service, staff member, date, time, price, status, history), messages from customers, notes you write, and staff names and schedules.
items.i6: Special categories: {brand} is not designed for special categories of data (such as health data). You will not enter them unless you are legally allowed to and have ensured the required safeguards; if you do, the security measures in this DPA apply to them too.

s3.title: Processing only on your instructions
s3.p1: We process the personal data only on your documented instructions, which are these Terms and this DPA, and the settings and actions you use in {brand}. We do not use it for our own purposes, sell it or combine it with other data, except where EU or Greek law requires us to process it; in that case we tell you first, unless the law forbids it.
s3.p2: We will inform you immediately if, in our opinion, an instruction infringes the GDPR or other data protection law.

s4.title: Confidentiality
s4.p1: Everyone authorised by us to access the personal data is bound by confidentiality and accesses it only as necessary to provide, secure or support the service.

s5.title: Security measures (article 32)
s5.p1: We implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, taking into account the state of the art, the cost and the risks. They currently include:

items.i1: Encryption in transit (HTTPS with HSTS; encrypted database connections).
items.i2: Encryption at rest provided by our hosting and database providers.
items.i3: Logical separation of each business’s data, enforced on every request, and role-based permissions for team members.
items.i4: Strong one-way password hashing, secure session cookies, login throttling and account lock-out, and rate limiting of sensitive actions.
items.i5: A content security policy and other security headers on every page.
items.i6: An audit log of significant account and data actions.
items.i7: Backups maintained by our database provider, allowing restoration after an incident.
items.i8: Access to production systems restricted to the provider’s owner, with multi-factor authentication on provider accounts.
items.i9: Data minimisation and automatic deletion as set out in our privacy policy.

s5.p2: We may update these measures as long as the overall level of security is not reduced.

s6.title: Sub-processors
s6.p1: You give us general authorisation to engage sub-processors. The sub-processors that process your customers’ data today are:
s6.p2: We impose data protection obligations on each sub-processor that are equivalent to those in this DPA and remain responsible to you for their performance. We will tell account owners by email at least 30 days before adding or replacing a sub-processor. You may object on reasonable data-protection grounds within that period; if we cannot reasonably address the objection, you may terminate the affected service and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

s7.title: International transfers
s7.p1: Where a sub-processor processes personal data outside the European Economic Area, we ensure the transfer complies with Chapter V of the GDPR, through an adequacy decision (such as the EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework for certified providers) or the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses with supplementary measures where needed.

s8.title: Helping you with data subject requests and compliance
s8.p1: {brand} lets you respond to most requests yourself: view, correct and export customer data, erase a customer, and delete your business. If we receive a request directly from one of your customers, we will not answer it ourselves (other than to redirect them) and will forward it to you without undue delay.
s8.p2: Taking into account the nature of the processing and the information available to us, we will also reasonably assist you with your obligations on security, breach notification, data protection impact assessments and prior consultation (GDPR articles 32–36).

s9.title: Personal data breaches
s9.p1: We will notify you without undue delay, and in any event within 48 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting your data, by email to the account owner. The notice will describe, as far as then known, the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of data subjects and records concerned, likely consequences, and the measures taken or proposed. We will take reasonable steps to contain the breach and provide further information as it becomes available, so that you can meet your own obligations to notify the supervisory authority and data subjects.

s10.title: Deletion and return of data
s10.p1: You can export your data at any time. When you erase a customer, their personal data is removed immediately and only anonymous appointment records remain for your statistics. When you delete your business, all its data is deleted from our live systems immediately. In both cases the data is overwritten in our database provider’s backups within 30 days, unless EU or Greek law requires us to keep it. If your subscription ends without you deleting your business, your data remains available to you until you delete it.

s11.title: Information and audits
s11.p1: We will make available the information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with article 28 GDPR, and answer your written questions about our processing. Where that is not sufficient, you may audit our compliance, including by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, with at least 30 days’ written notice, no more than once a year (unless required by a supervisory authority or after a breach), during business hours and in a way that does not compromise other customers’ data or our security. Each party bears its own costs.

s12.title: Liability and term
s12.p1: Liability under this DPA is subject to the limitations in the Terms, except where the law does not allow them. This DPA ends automatically when we no longer process personal data on your behalf; the obligations on deletion and confidentiality continue until then. It is governed by the same law and courts as the Terms.

s13.title: Contact
s13.p1: Questions about this DPA or requests to receive a countersigned copy: <email>{email}</email>.
